danish.title: Sjette bog (1808–10) — Kapitel 10
paragraphs: Pierre fortsatte sin dagbog, og her er, hvad han skrev i denne tid:
Den 24. november

Stod op klokken otte, læste i Skriften og gik derefter til mine pligter. (På Josef Aleksejevitjs råd var Pierre gået i statens tjeneste og tjente i en af komitéerne.) Kom hjem til middag og spiste alene — grevinden havde mange gæster, jeg ikke bryder mig om. Jeg spiste og drak med måde og kopierede efter middagen nogle passager for brødrene. Om aftenen gik jeg ned til grevinden og fortalte en morsom historie om B., og huskede først, at jeg ikke burde have gjort det, da alle lo højt.

Jeg går i seng med et lykkeligt og roligt sind. Store Gud, hjælp mig at vandre ad Dine veje, (1) at besejre vrede med ro og besindighed, (2) at overvinde begær med selvbeherskelse og afsky, (3) at trække mig tilbage fra verdslighedens larm, men ikke undgå (a) tjenesten for staten, (b) familiepligter, (c) omgang med mine venner og forvaltningen af mine sager.
Den 27. november

Stod sent op. Da jeg vågnede, blev jeg længe liggende og gav efter for dovenskab. O Gud, hjælp og styrk mig, at jeg må vandre ad Dine veje! Læste i Skriften, men uden den rette følelse. Broder Urusov kom, og vi talte om verdslige tomheder. Han fortalte mig om kejserens nye planer. Jeg begyndte at kritisere dem, men huskede mine regler og min velgørers ord — at en sand frimurer bør være en nidkær arbejder for staten, når hans hjælp kræves, og en stille tilskuer, når der ikke kaldes på ham. Min tunge er min fjende. Brødrene G. V. og O. besøgte mig, og vi havde en indledende samtale om optagelsen af en ny broder. De overdrog mig pligten som retor. Jeg føler mig svag og uværdig. Derefter drejede vores samtale sig om fortolkningen af templets syv søjler og trin, de syv videnskaber, de syv dyder, de syv laster og Helligåndens syv gaver. Broder O. var meget veltalende. Om aftenen fandt optagelsen sted. Den nye udsmykning af lokalerne bidrog meget til skuets pragt. Det var Boris Drubetskoj, der blev optaget. Jeg indstillede ham og var retor. En mærkelig følelse oprørte mig hele den tid, jeg var alene med ham i det mørke kammer. Jeg greb mig selv i at nære en følelse af had til ham, som jeg forgæves forsøgte at overvinde. Derfor ville jeg virkelig gerne frelse ham fra det onde og lede ham ind på sandhedens vej, men onde tanker om ham forlod mig ikke. Det forekom mig, at hans formål med at indtræde i broderskabet blot var at opnå fortrolighed og yndest hos vores loges medlemmer. Bortset fra at han flere gange havde spurgt mig, om N. og S. var medlemmer af vores loge (et spørgsmål, jeg ikke kunne besvare), og at han efter mine iagttagelser er ude af stand til at føle ærbødighed for vores hellige orden og er for optaget af og tilfreds med det ydre menneske til at ønske åndelig forbedring, havde jeg ingen grund til at tvivle på ham; men han forekom mig uoprigtig, og hele den tid jeg stod alene med ham i det mørke tempel, forekom det mig, at han smilede foragteligt ad mine ord, og jeg ønskede virkelig at stikke hans blottede bryst med det sværd, jeg holdt mod det. Jeg kunne ikke være veltalende, og jeg kunne heller ikke åbent nævne mine tvivl for brødrene og stormesteren. Store Arkitekt af Naturen, hjælp mig at finde den sande vej ud af løgnens labyrint!
Herefter var tre sider i dagbogen tomme, og derefter var følgende skrevet:

Jeg har haft en lang og lærerig samtale alene med broder V., som rådede mig til at holde fast ved broder A. Skønt jeg er uværdig, blev meget åbenbaret for mig. Adonai er navnet på verdens skaber. Elohim er navnet på alles hersker. Det tredje navn er det uudsigelige navn, som betyder det Alt. Samtaler med broder V. styrker, forfrisker og støtter mig på dydens vej. I hans nærværelse har tvivlen ingen plads. Forskellen mellem de verdslige videnskabers fattige lærdomme og vores hellige, altomfattende lære er mig klar. De menneskelige videnskaber sønderdeler alt for at forstå det og dræber alt for at undersøge det. I vores ordens hellige videnskab er alt ét, alt kendes i sin helhed og i livet. Treenigheden — stoflets tre elementer — er svovl, kviksølv og salt. Svovl er af olieagtig og ildagtig natur; i forbindelse med salt vækker det ved sin ildagtige natur et begær i dette, hvorved det tiltrækker kviksølv, griber det, fastholder det, og frembringer i forening andre legemer. Kviksølv er en flydende, flygtig, åndelig essens. Kristus, Helligånden, Ham!...
Den 3. december

Vågnede sent, læste i Skriften, men var apatisk. Gik derefter op og ned i den store hal. Ville meditere, men i stedet malede min fantasi en hændelse for fire år siden, da Dolokhov mødte mig i Moskva efter vores duel og sagde, at han håbede, jeg nød fuldkommen sindsro trods min kones fravær. Dengang svarede jeg ham ikke. Nu genkaldte jeg hvert eneste detalje i dette møde og gav ham i tankerne de mest ondskabsfulde og bitre svar. Jeg besindede mig og drev den tanke bort, først da jeg opdagede, at jeg glødede af vrede, men jeg angrede ikke tilstrækkeligt. Derefter kom Boris Drubetskoj og begyndte at berette forskellige oplevelser. Hans komme irriterede mig fra starten, og jeg sagde noget ubehageligt til ham. Han svarede. Jeg brusede op og sagde meget, der var ubehageligt og endda uhøfligt. Han blev tavs, og jeg besindede mig, først da det var for sent. Min Gud, jeg kan slet ikke komme overens med ham. Årsagen er min egoisme. Jeg sætter mig over ham og bliver derved langt værre end han, for han er overbærende med min grovhed, mens jeg tværtimod nærer foragt for ham. O Gud, giv at jeg i hans nærværelse snarere må se min egen usselhed og opføre mig, så også han drager nytte af det. Efter middagen faldt jeg i søvn, og mens jeg døsede hen, hørte jeg tydeligt en stemme sige i mit venstre øre: »Din dag!«

Jeg drømte, at jeg gik i mørket og pludselig blev omringet af hunde, men jeg gik videre uforfærdet. Pludselig greb en lille hund fat i mit venstre lår med tænderne og ville ikke slippe. Jeg begyndte at kvæle den med mine hænder. Næppe havde jeg revet den løs, før en anden, større hund begyndte at bide mig. Jeg løftede den op, men jo højere jeg løftede den, desto større og tungere blev den. Og pludselig kom broder A. og tog min arm og førte mig til en bygning, til hvilken vi måtte passere hen over en smal planke. Jeg trådte ud på den, men den bøjede sig og gav efter, og jeg begyndte at klatre op ad et hegn, som jeg næppe kunne nå med hænderne. Efter stor anstrengelse hev jeg mig op, så mit ben hang ned på den ene side og min krop på den anden. Jeg så mig omkring og så broder A. stå på hegnet og pege mod en bred allé og en have, og i haven var en stor og smuk bygning. Jeg vågnede. O Herre, store Naturens Arkitekt, hjælp mig at rive disse hunde — mine lidenskaber — fra mig, især den sidste, som i sig forener styrken af alle de foregående, og hjælp mig at betræde det dydens tempel, til hvis syn jeg nåede i min drøm.
Den 7. december

Jeg drømte, at Josef Aleksejevitj sad i mit hus, og at jeg var meget glad og ønskede at underholde ham. Det forekom mig, at jeg plaprede ustandseligt med andre, og pludselig huskede jeg, at dette ikke kunne glæde ham, og jeg ønskede at komme tæt på ham og omfavne ham. Men så snart jeg nærmede mig, så jeg, at hans ansigt var forandret og blevet ungt, og han fortalte mig stille noget om vores ordens lære, men så sagte, at jeg ikke kunne høre det. Så forekom det mig, at vi alle forlod rummet, og noget mærkeligt skete. Vi sad eller lå på gulvet. Han fortalte mig noget, og jeg ønskede at vise ham min følsomhed, og uden at lytte til, hvad han sagde, begyndte jeg at forestille mig tilstanden i mit indre menneske og Guds nåde, der helliggjorde mig. Og tårer trillede ned ad mine kinder, og jeg var glad for, at han bemærkede det. Men han så på mig med irritation og sprang op og afbrød sine bemærkninger. Jeg følte mig flov og spurgte, om det, han havde sagt, ikke vedrørte mig; men han svarede ikke, gav mig et venligt blik, og så befandt vi os pludselig i mit soveværelse, hvor der er en dobbeltseng. Han lagde sig på kanten af den, og jeg brændte af længsel efter at kærtegne ham og lægge mig også. Og han sagde: »Sig mig ærligt, hvad er din største fristelse? Kender du den? Jeg tror, du allerede kender den.« Flov over spørgsmålet svarede jeg, at dovenskab var min største fristelse. Han rystede vantro på hovedet; og endnu mere flov sagde jeg, at skønt jeg levede med min kone, som han havde rådet, levede jeg ikke med hende som hendes ægtemand. Dertil svarede han, at man ikke bør nægte sin kone sine omfavnelser, og gav mig at forstå, at det var min pligt. Men jeg svarede, at jeg ville skamme mig over at gøre det, og pludselig forsvandt alting. Og jeg vågnede og fandt i mit sind teksten fra Evangeliet: »Livet var menneskers lys. Og lyset skinner i mørket, og mørket begreb det ikke.« Josef Aleksejevitjs ansigt havde set ungt og strålende ud. Den dag modtog jeg et brev fra min velgører, hvori han skrev om »ægteskabelige pligter.«
Den 9. december

Jeg havde en drøm, fra hvilken jeg vågnede med bankende hjerte. Jeg drømte, at jeg var i Moskva i mit hus, i den store stue, og Josef Aleksejevitj kom ind fra salonen. Jeg syntes straks at vide, at genfødslens proces allerede havde fundet sted i ham, og jeg styrtede hen for at møde ham. Jeg omfavnede ham og kyssede hans hænder, og han sagde: »Har du bemærket, at mit ansigt er anderledes?« Jeg betragtede ham, idet jeg stadig holdt ham i mine arme, og så, at hans ansigt var ungt, men at han intet hår havde på hovedet, og hans træk var helt forandrede. Og jeg sagde: »Jeg ville have genkendt dig, hvis jeg havde mødt dig tilfældigt,« og tænkte ved mig selv: »Taler jeg sandt?« Og pludselig så jeg ham ligge som et lig; derefter kom han sig gradvist og gik med mig ind i mit studerekammer med en stor bog af tegneark; jeg sagde: »Det har jeg tegnet,« og han svarede med et nik. Jeg åbnede bogen, og på alle siderne var der fortræffelige tegninger. Og i min drøm vidste jeg, at disse tegninger forestillede sjælens kærlighedseventyr med sin elskede. Og på siderne så jeg en smuk skildring af en jomfru i gennemsigtigt gevandt og med en gennemsigtig krop, der fløj op mod skyerne. Og jeg syntes at vide, at denne jomfru intet andet var end en fremstilling af Højsangen. Og idet jeg betragtede disse tegninger, drømte jeg, at jeg forbrød mig, men ikke kunne rive mig løs. Herre, hjælp mig! Min Gud, hvis Din forladelse af mig er Din vilje, så ske Din vilje; men er det mig selv, der er årsagen, så lær mig, hvad jeg bør gøre! Jeg vil gå til grunde i min udsvævelse, hvis Du fuldstændig forlader mig!

english.title: Book Six (1808 - 10) — Chapter 10
paragraphs: Pierre continued with his diary, and this is what he wrote during that time:
24th November

Got up at eight, read the Scriptures, then went to my duties. (On Joseph Alexeevich's advice, Pierre had entered government service and was working on one of the committees.) Came home for dinner and dined alone — the countess had many visitors I don't care for. I ate and drank in moderation and after dinner copied out some passages for the Brothers. In the evening I went down to the countess and told a funny story about B., and only remembered afterwards that I shouldn't have done so when everybody burst out laughing.

I am going to bed with a happy and peaceful mind. Great God, help me to walk in Your ways: (1) to conquer anger through calm and deliberation, (2) to overcome lust through self-discipline and repulsion, (3) to withdraw from worldliness, but not to avoid (a) the service of the state, (b) family duties, (c) relations with friends, and the management of my affairs.
27th November

Got up late. When I woke I lay a long time in bed, giving in to laziness. O God, help me and strengthen me to walk in Your ways! Read the Scriptures, but without proper feeling. Brother Urusov came. We talked about the vanities of the world. He told me about the Emperor’s new projects. I began to criticize them but recalled my rules and my benefactor’s words: a true Freemason works zealously for the state when his help is needed and looks quietly on when nobody asks it of him. My tongue is my enemy. Brothers G. V. and O. called, and we had a first discussion about admitting a new Brother. They gave me the office of Rhetor. I feel weak and unworthy. We spoke of the meaning of the Temple’s seven pillars and steps, the seven sciences, the seven virtues, the seven vices and the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. Brother O. spoke very well. The admission took place this evening. The new decorations in the lodge greatly added to the splendor of the ceremony. It was Boris Drubetskoy we admitted. I nominated him and acted as Rhetor. All the time I stood alone with him in the dark chamber I felt strangely agitated. I caught myself hating him and tried in vain to overcome it. For that very reason I long to save him from evil and set him on the path of truth, but the evil thoughts about him persisted. I felt he had joined the Brotherhood simply to make friends and gain favor with members of our lodge. He had asked me several times whether N. and S. were members, a question I could not answer. To my eyes he is incapable of respect for our holy order and far too taken up and pleased with the outward man to want to improve his soul. Apart from that I had no cause to doubt him. Yet he struck me as insincere. All the time we stood alone in the dark temple I fancied he was smiling contemptuously at my words, and I truly wanted to plunge into his bare breast the sword I held against it. I could neither speak with eloquence nor tell the Brothers and the Grand Master frankly of my doubts. Great Architect of Nature, help me find the true path out of this labyrinth of lies!
After this, three pages were left blank in the diary, and then the following was written:

I had a long and instructive conversation alone with Brother V., who advised me to hold fast by Brother A. Though I am unworthy, much was revealed to me. Adonai is the name of the creator of the world. Elohim is the name of the ruler of all. The third name is the unutterable name which means the All. Conversations with Brother V. strengthen, refresh, and support me on the path of virtue. In his presence doubt has no place. The distinction between the shallow teachings of worldly science and our sacred all-embracing teaching is clear to me. Human sciences dissect everything to understand it, and kill everything to examine it. In the holy science of our order all is one, all is known in its completeness and life. The Trinity — the three elements of matter — are sulphur, mercury, and salt. Sulphur is of an oily and fiery nature; in combination with salt, by its fiery nature it arouses a desire in the latter by means of which it attracts mercury, seizes it, holds it, and in combination produces other substances. Mercury is a fluid, volatile, spiritual essence. Christ, the Holy Spirit, Him!...
3rd December

Woke late, read the Scriptures but felt listless. Afterward went and paced up and down the large hall. I wanted to meditate, but instead my imagination kept picturing something that happened four years ago, when Dolokhov ran into me in Moscow after our duel and said he hoped I was enjoying perfect peace of mind despite my wife's absence. At the time I gave him no answer. Now I recalled every detail of that encounter and in my mind gave him the most vicious and bitter replies. I caught myself and pushed the thought away only when I realized I was burning with anger — but I didn't repent enough. Then Boris Drubetskoy came and began telling various stories. His visit irritated me from the start, and I said something unpleasant to him. He responded. I flared up and said much that was rude and even cruel to him. He fell silent, and I came to my senses only when it was too late. My God, I cannot get along with him at all. The cause of this is my own selfishness. I set myself above him and so become much worse than he, for he is patient with my rudeness while I on the contrary harbor contempt for him. O God, grant that in his presence I may see my own failings, and behave so that he too may benefit. After dinner I fell asleep, and as I was dozing off I clearly heard a voice in my left ear saying: "Your day!"

I dreamed I was walking in the dark and was suddenly surrounded by dogs, but I went on without fear. Suddenly a small dog seized my left thigh with its teeth and wouldn't let go. I began to choke it with my hands. No sooner had I torn it off than another, bigger one, began biting me. I lifted it up, but the higher I lifted it the bigger and heavier it grew. Then Brother A. appeared and, taking my arm, led me to a building we could only enter by walking along a narrow plank. I stepped on it, but it bent and gave way and I began to climb a fence I could barely reach with my hands. After much effort I dragged myself up, so that my leg hung down on one side and my body on the other. I looked around and saw Brother A. standing on the fence, pointing me toward a broad avenue and garden, and in the garden was a large and beautiful building. I woke up. O Lord, great Architect of Nature, help me to tear from myself these dogs — my passions, especially the last, which combines in itself the strength of all the others — and help me enter that temple of virtue which I glimpsed in my dream.
7th December

I dreamed that Joseph Alexeevich was sitting in my house, and that I was very glad and wanted to make him welcome. It seemed as if I was chattering endlessly with other people and suddenly remembered that this could not please him, and I wished to go close to him and embrace him. But as soon as I drew near, I saw that his face had changed and grown young, and he was quietly telling me something about the teachings of our order, but so softly that I couldn't hear. Then it seemed we all left the room and something strange happened. We were sitting or lying on the floor. He was telling me something, and I wished to show him my sensitivity, and not listening to what he was saying I began imagining the state of my inner man and the grace of God sanctifying me. Tears came to my eyes, and I was glad he noticed. But he looked at me with annoyance and jumped up, breaking off his remarks. I felt ashamed and asked whether what he'd been saying didn't concern me; but he didn't reply, gave me a kind look, and then we suddenly found ourselves in my bedroom where there is a double bed. He lay down on the edge of it and I burned with longing to be close to him and lie down too. And he said: "Tell me honestly, what is your chief temptation? Do you know it? I think you know it already." Embarrassed by this question, I answered that laziness was my chief temptation. He shook his head in disbelief; and even more ashamed, I said that though I was living with my wife as he had advised, I was not living with her as her husband. To this he replied that one should not deprive a wife of one's embraces, and gave me to understand that that was my duty. But I answered that I would be ashamed to do it, and suddenly everything vanished. I woke up and found in my mind the text from the Gospel: "The life was the light of men. And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not." Joseph Alexeevich's face had looked young and bright. That day I received a letter from my benefactor in which he wrote about "conjugal duties."
9th December

I had a dream from which I awoke with a pounding heart. I saw that I was in Moscow in my house, in the large sitting room, and Joseph Alexeevich came in from the drawing room. I seemed to know at once that the process of spiritual renewal had already taken place in him, and I rushed to meet him. I embraced him and kissed his hands, and he said: "Have you noticed that my face is different?" I looked at him, still holding him in my arms, and saw that his face was young, but that he had no hair on his head and his features were completely changed. And I said: "I would have known you if I'd met you by chance." And I thought to myself: "Am I telling the truth?" And suddenly I saw him lying like a dead body; then he gradually recovered and went with me into my study carrying a large book of drawing paper. I said: "I drew that," and he answered by bowing his head. I opened the book, and on every page there were beautiful drawings. And in my dream I knew that these drawings represented the love adventures of the soul with its beloved. And on the pages I saw a beautiful image of a maiden in transparent garments and with a transparent body, flying up to the clouds. And I seemed to know that this maiden was nothing other than a representation of the Song of Songs. And looking at those drawings I felt that I was doing wrong, but could not tear myself away from them. Lord, help me! My God, if Your forsaking me is Your doing, then Your will be done; but if I am myself the cause, teach me what I should do! I will be destroyed by my depravity if You utterly desert me!
